magnesium_ob.title: Magnesium sulfate (preeclampsia, eclampsia, fetal neuroprotection)
sections: Seizure **prevention** in preeclampsia with severe features and **treatment** of eclamptic seizures; also fetal neuroprotection before 32 weeks. It is **not** a blood pressure drug: severe BP still needs labetalol, hydralazine or nifedipine ✅✅ [PB 222; CO 767].
Blocks calcium at nerve endings and NMDA receptors in the brain, calming overexcited neurons; also relaxes smooth muscle. The same calcium blocking is why toxicity weakens reflexes, then breathing.
Approved dose (and where it comes from)

**IV:** load 4 to 6 g, then 1 to 2 g/h. The premixed bag label says load over 15 minutes; ACOG and the eclampsia checklist use 20 to 30 minutes ✅✅ [bag label; ACOG checklist; PB 222].
**IM (no IV access):** 10 g of 50% solution (5 g in each buttock), then 4 to 5 g IM into alternate buttocks every 4 hours as needed ✅✅ [vial label; ACOG checklist].
**Seizure while on magnesium:** extra 2 to 4 g IV over 5 minutes ✅ [PB 222].
**Maximum:** 30 to 40 g in 24 hours; with severe renal insufficiency 20 g per 48 hours with frequent levels ✅✅ [vial label; bag label].
**Fetal neuroprotection:** 6 g over 20 to 30 minutes, then 2 g/h up to 12 hours (BEAM based protocol) ✅ [CO 455; MAHEC protocol].

**No.** Magnesium for preeclampsia is a **fixed dose** (grams), not mg/kg. Obese patients may reach lower levels on the same dose, which is one reason some teams use 2 g/h rather than 1 g/h and check levels ⚠️ [VERIFY St. Mary's protocol].

**1 g magnesium sulfate = 8.12 mEq magnesium** ✅ [vial label].
Example bag 20 g in 500 mL = **40 mg/mL** (check the bag you actually stock ⚠️):
• 6 g load = 6,000 mg ÷ 40 mg/mL = **150 mL**; over 20 minutes = 150 × 3 = **450 mL/h** for 20 minutes.
• 2 g/h maintenance = 2,000 mg ÷ 40 = **50 mL/h**; 1 g/h = **25 mL/h**.
• 24 hour total at 2 g/h after a 6 g load = 6 + 48 = **54 g**: above the 30 to 40 g per 24 h label maximum. Standard OB practice runs these doses; flag it as a reason levels and close monitoring matter, and follow the order set ⚠️.
Example bag 4 g in 100 mL (40 mg/mL): the load is the same mL; many sites hang the load as its own bag so the pump cannot run the whole bag by mistake.

**Never IV push** concentrated solution. The vial label says IV injection generally should not exceed **150 mg/min**, except in severe eclampsia with seizures; the obstetric load (4 to 6 g over 15 to 30 minutes, about 130 to 400 mg/min) is the recognized exception ✅ [vial label].
The 50% vial must be **diluted to 20% or less** for IV use ✅ [vial label].
Use a **premixed bag, a dedicated pump channel**, and program the load and maintenance separately (bolus feature or a separate load bag), with an **independent double check** ✅ [ISMP high alert].
Keep magnesium bags physically apart from oxytocin bags (look alike, both on L&D pumps) ✅ [ISMP].

**Contraindicated:** myasthenia gravis, heart block or myocardial damage (label also lists diabetic coma) ✅ [bag label].
**Renal failure:** the ACOG eclampsia checklist lists it as a contraindication; the label instead allows reduced dosing (4 g load, 1 g/h, max 20 g per 48 h) with frequent levels. This is a team decision ✅✅ [ACOG checklist; bag label].
**Pregnancy duration:** continuous use beyond 5 to 7 days can cause fetal low calcium and bone problems ✅ [bag label].

**Nifedipine and other calcium channel blockers:** label warns against combining (hypotension, neuromuscular effects); ACOG still uses nifedipine for severe BP with close monitoring ✅✅ [bag label; CO 767].
**Neuromuscular blockers** (rocuronium, succinylcholine): effect is prolonged; tell anesthesia she is on magnesium.
**Aminoglycosides** (gentamicin): add neuromuscular blockade and kidney risk.
**CNS depressants** (opioids, sedatives): additive respiratory depression.

Magnesium is cleared **only by the kidneys**. Before verifying, look at SCr and **urine output (goal at least 100 mL per 4 hours, about 25 mL/h)** ✅✅ [bag label; ACOG checklist]. Report urine output below 30 mL/h ✅ [ACOG checklist].

Deep tendon (patellar) reflexes present; respiratory rate at least 16 (label) and act if below 12; urine output at least 100 mL per 4 hours; mental status, SpO2; serum magnesium if kidneys are impaired, symptoms appear or seizures recur ✅✅ [bag label; PB 222].
**Target serum level:** 2.5 to 5 mEq/L (3 to 6 mg/dL) per label; ACOG sources quote about 4.8 to 8.4 mg/dL, so know which units your lab reports ⚠️ [VERIFY lab].

Reflexes weaken above about **4 mEq/L**; may be absent at **10 mEq/L**, when respiratory paralysis is a risk ✅ [bag label].
**Action:** stop the infusion, support breathing, **calcium gluconate 1 g IV (10 mL of 10%) over 2 to 3 minutes**, STAT magnesium level and creatinine ✅✅ [ACOG checklist (1 to 2 min); CO 767 (3 min)]. Keep calcium gluconate at the bedside before starting.

**Urine output 15 mL/h?** Still give the **loading dose** (it fills body water and does not depend on kidneys), then **lower or hold the maintenance**, check a level within a few hours and every 4 to 6 hours, and reassess reflexes and breathing hourly; label: 4 g load then 1 g/h, max 20 g per 48 h ✅ [bag label]. Call the OB now (below 30 mL/h). If true renal failure: discuss an alternative (below) ⚠️ [VERIFY order set].
**No IV?** IM 10 g (5 g each buttock), then 5 g IM every 4 hours ✅✅.
**Seizure despite magnesium?** 2 to 4 g IV over 5 minutes; if still seizing, lorazepam ✅.
**Going to cesarean?** Continue through surgery; tell anesthesia (paralytics last longer).
**Breastfeeding?** Compatible ✅ [LactMed].
Alternatives when magnesium cannot be used

Magnesium is clearly better than phenytoin or diazepam for preventing and treating eclamptic seizures, so alternatives are only for contraindications (for example myasthenia gravis) ✅ [PB 222].
ACOG eclampsia checklist options: **lorazepam 2 to 4 mg IV** once (may repeat once after 10 to 15 min); **diazepam 5 to 10 mg IV** every 5 to 10 minutes (max 30 mg); **phenytoin 15 to 20 mg/kg IV** (may repeat 10 mg/kg after 20 min; avoid with hypotension); **levetiracetam 500 mg IV or PO**, may repeat in 12 hours (adjust for kidneys) ✅ [ACOG checklist]. Choose with OB and neurology.
Usually **24 hours after delivery** (or 24 hours after the last seizure) ✅ [PB 222].
Crosses the placenta: newborn may have low tone, weak reflexes and slow breathing; tell the pediatric team ✅ [bag label].
Who to call and what to document
OB for dose, urine output and BP; anesthesia for any surgery or epidural; nursing for the monitoring schedule. Document the load time, maintenance rate, levels and any change.
Product and concentration stocked, pump library limits, order set for renal adjustment and IM backup, where calcium gluconate is kept.

labetalol_ob.title: Labetalol IV and PO (pregnancy and postpartum BP)
sections: Acute severe range BP (160 or more systolic or 110 or more diastolic for 15 minutes) in pregnancy and postpartum; also oral treatment of chronic hypertension ✅✅ [CO 767; ACC].
Blocks beta receptors and alpha 1 receptors (IV ratio about 1:7 alpha to beta): lowers BP without reflex tachycardia.

**IV:** 20 mg over 2 minutes; recheck BP in 10 minutes; if still severe 40 mg, then 80 mg, each with a 10 minute recheck. If still severe after 80 mg, switch to hydralazine and get help ✅✅ [CO 767; algorithm]. The injection label caps cumulative repeated doses at 300 mg ⚠️ [label].
**Oral (chronic or step down):** usually 200 to 2,400 mg per day divided 2 to 3 times ✅ [ACC].
Each IV dose over 2 minutes. Patient lying down during and after (orthostatic hypotension).

Asthma or reactive airway disease, heart block beyond first degree or significant bradycardia, decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock. Algorithm: if HR is under 60 or she has asthma, start with hydralazine or nifedipine; if HR is over 110, labetalol is preferred ✅ [algorithm].
Additive hypotension with magnesium, nifedipine, anesthesia. Masks hypoglycemia signs in diabetics.
BP every 10 minutes during dosing, maternal heart rate, fetal heart rate tracing. Goal is not normal BP: about 130 to 150 systolic and 80 to 100 diastolic ✅ [algorithm].
Can cause neonatal bradycardia and hypoglycemia; tell the pediatric team. Compatible with breastfeeding ✅ [ACC; LactMed].
Hydralazine IV or immediate release nifedipine PO (all three are first line) ✅✅ [CO 767].

hydralazine_ob.title: Hydralazine IV (pregnancy and postpartum BP)
sections: First line for acute severe range BP, especially with asthma or bradycardia ✅✅ [CO 767; algorithm].
Directly relaxes arterial smooth muscle. Reflex tachycardia is common.
5 to 10 mg IV (or IM) over 2 minutes; recheck in 20 minutes; if still severe, 10 mg; if still severe after that, switch to labetalol (unless contraindicated) and get help ✅✅ [CO 767; algorithm].
Peaks 10 to 20 minutes, which is why the recheck is at 20 minutes, not 10.
Overshoot hypotension (can drop placental blood flow and cause fetal heart rate changes), maternal tachycardia, headache (can mimic worsening preeclampsia).
BP every 5 to 10 minutes after dosing, maternal heart rate, fetal heart rate.
Labetalol IV or nifedipine IR PO.

nifedipine_ob.title: Nifedipine (immediate release for severe BP; extended release for chronic)
sections: IR: acute severe range BP, very useful without IV access. ER: chronic hypertension in pregnancy and postpartum ✅✅ [CO 767; ACC].

**IR:** 10 mg PO; recheck in 20 minutes; if still severe 20 mg; recheck 20 minutes; 20 mg again; if still severe, switch to labetalol and get help ✅✅ [CO 767; algorithm].
**ER:** often 30 to 120 mg once daily ✅ [ACC].
**Swallow whole.** Never sublingual, never bitten or punctured: the BP can crash and drop blood flow to the baby.
Magnesium: label warns about combining with calcium channel blockers; ACOG still uses both with close BP and reflex monitoring. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise levels.

oxytocin.title: Oxytocin (induction, augmentation, postpartum hemorrhage)
sections: Induction and augmentation of labor; first line prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage from uterine atony ✅✅ [PB 183; PB 107].

**Induction, low dose:** start 0.5 to 2 milliunits/min, increase by 1 to 2 milliunits/min every 15 to 40 minutes ✅ [PB 107; summary].
**High dose regimen:** start 6, increase by 3 to 6 milliunits/min ✅ [PB 107].
**PPH:** 10 to 40 units in 500 to 1,000 mL IV as a continuous infusion, or 10 units IM ✅✅ [PB 183; summary].

Example standard bag 30 units in 500 mL = 60 milliunits/mL (check St. Mary's bag ⚠️). 2 milliunits/min = 2 / 60 x 60 min = **2 mL/h**. 10 milliunits/min = **10 mL/h**. In milliunits/min with this bag, mL/h equals milliunits/min.
ISMP high alert drug: one standard concentration, smart pump library, never next to magnesium bags. Avoid rapid undiluted IV push (hypotension, tachycardia) ⚠️ [label].

Tachysystole (more than 5 contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes) with fetal heart rate changes: lower or stop. Water intoxication and low sodium with long, high dose infusions (oxytocin acts like ADH) ✅ [summary].
Methylergonovine, carboprost, misoprostol, plus TXA (see their cards).

gbs_abx.title: GBS intrapartum prophylaxis (penicillin, ampicillin, cefazolin, clindamycin, vancomycin)
sections: Positive GBS culture at 36 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks; GBS bacteriuria any time this pregnancy; a prior infant with invasive GBS; unknown status with labor under 37 weeks, membranes ruptured 18 hours or more, temperature 38 °C or higher, or a positive rapid test ✅✅ [CO 797].

(No anaphylaxis, angioedema, respiratory distress, hives, or severe skin reaction): **cefazolin** 2 g IV, then 1 g every 8 hours ✅✅ [CO 797].

**Clindamycin** 900 mg IV every 8 hours only if the isolate is susceptible (including inducible resistance testing); otherwise **vancomycin** 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, maximum 2 g per dose ✅✅ [CO 797].
Vancomycin for 72 kg: 20 x 72 = 1,440 mg, round per protocol (for example 1,500 mg). Infusion at no faster than 10 mg/min = at least 150 minutes per label ⚠️ [St. Mary's infusion policy].
Penicillin, ampicillin or cefazolin started at least 4 hours before delivery ✅ [CO 797]. Clindamycin and vancomycin do not count as adequate.

vancomycin.title: Vancomycin IV (and oral)
sections: Serious gram positive infections, especially MRSA (bacteremia, pneumonia, osteomyelitis, meningitis), and empiric coverage when MRSA is likely. **Oral** vancomycin only treats C. difficile ✅✅ [Rybak; IDSA 2021].
Binds the D-Ala-D-Ala end of cell wall building blocks; too big to cross gram negative outer membranes. Kills slowly; total exposure (AUC) predicts success.
AUC over 24 hours **400 to 600** (assuming MIC 1), by Bayesian software (preferred) or two levels; trough only dosing to 15 to 20 is no longer recommended for serious MRSA ✅ [Rybak].

**Load:** 20 to 35 mg/kg **actual** body weight, max 3,000 mg; obese 20 to 25 mg/kg, max 3,000 mg. **Maintenance:** 15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours with normal kidneys; obese usually 4,500 mg/day or less to start. **Children 3 months+:** 60 to 80 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours. **Continuous infusion:** load 15 to 20 mg/kg, then 30 to 40 mg/kg/day (up to 60), target level 20 to 25. **Hemodialysis (after session):** load 25 mg/kg, then 7.5 mg/kg (low permeability) or 10 mg/kg (high permeability) after each session, pre dialysis levels at least weekly ✅ [Rybak].

1. ke = ln(C1 / C2) / hours between draws. 2. Half life = 0.693 / ke. 3. Back extrapolate the true peak to the end of the infusion: Cmax = C1 x e^(ke x t). 4. Forward extrapolate the true trough to the end of the interval. 5. AUC per dose = infusion time x (Cmax + Cmin) / 2 + (Cmax minus Cmin) / ke. 6. AUC24 = AUC per dose x doses per day. 7. New dose = old dose x target AUC / current AUC (linear).

Label: at least 60 minutes and no faster than 10 mg/min, whichever is longer (1,500 mg = 150 minutes). Many hospitals use a 1 g per hour policy ⚠️ [St. Mary's]. Too fast causes the **vancomycin infusion reaction** (flushing, itching, low BP): a rate reaction, not an allergy.

Cleared by the kidneys. Kidney injury rises with AUC above 600, long courses, and other nephrotoxins (contrast, loop diuretics, aminoglycosides; piperacillin tazobactam has been reported to raise risk, mostly observational data) ✅ [Rybak]. Ototoxicity is rare.
SCr at least daily early, urine output, AUC within 24 to 48 hours for serious infection, and again when kidney function or the dose changes ✅ [Rybak].

**Kidneys failing?** Same load; longer interval or smaller dose; level based dosing. **Flushing?** Pause, antihistamine, restart slower. **MRSA nares negative in pneumonia?** Consider stopping. **MSSA in blood?** Switch to cefazolin or nafcillin.

Linezolid (pneumonia, skin; watch platelets and serotonergic drugs), daptomycin (not for pneumonia), ceftaroline. For C. diff: fidaxomicin or oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days ✅ [IDSA 2021].

aminoglycoside.title: Gentamicin and tobramycin (aminoglycosides)
sections: Serious gram negative infections, often combined with a beta lactam; low dose gentamicin for gram positive synergy (enterococcal endocarditis).
Bind the 30S ribosome; uptake needs oxygen, so no anaerobic activity. **Concentration dependent killing with a post antibiotic effect**: high peak, then a drug free gap.

Ideal body weight (men 50 kg, women 45.5 kg, + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 feet). If actual is more than about 120% of ideal, use adjusted = IBW + 0.4 x (actual minus IBW). If actual is below ideal, use actual ⚠️ [protocol].

7 mg/kg once; one random level 6 to 14 hours after the start; plot for every 24, 36 or 48 hours; on a line pick the longer; above the q48h zone stop scheduled doses and redose when below 1 mcg/mL ✅ [Nicolau 1995]. **Not for:** pregnancy, burns over 20%, ascites, CrCl below 20 or dialysis, endocarditis synergy, cystic fibrosis, children ✅ [Nicolau].

Label: 3 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours (up to 5 mg/kg/day for life threatening infection). Peak 30 minutes after the end of a 30 minute infusion; trough just before the next dose. Avoid peaks above 12 and troughs above 2 mcg/mL ✅ [label].
About 3 mg/kg/day divided (for example 1 mg/kg every 8 hours), peak 3 to 4, trough below 1 ✅ [AHA 2015]. For E. faecalis, ampicillin plus ceftriaxone avoids aminoglycoside toxicity ✅ [AHA 2015].
Kidney injury (usually reversible), ototoxicity (hearing and balance, often permanent), neuromuscular blockade ✅ [label]. Ask about ringing ears and dizziness every day.
Loop diuretics (ears), vancomycin, amphotericin, contrast, NSAIDs (kidneys), neuromuscular blockers and magnesium (paralysis).

**Rising creatinine?** Get a level, lengthen the interval or stop. **Ringing ears?** Call today; switch if cultures allow. **Obese?** Adjusted weight. **Neonate?** Unit chart by GA or PMA and PNA, never Hartford.
A beta lactam alone when susceptible; fluoroquinolones; for synergy in E. faecalis endocarditis, ampicillin plus ceftriaxone.

doacs.title: DOACs: apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban
sections: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban: direct factor Xa inhibitors. Dabigatran: direct thrombin inhibitor. No routine INR monitoring.

**AF:** 5 mg BID; 2.5 mg BID only with **2 of 3**: age 80+, weight 60 kg or less, SCr 1.5+. **VTE:** 10 mg BID x 7 days, then 5 mg BID; after 6 months, 2.5 mg BID for extended treatment (CHEST 2021). Tablets may be crushed (water, D5W, apple juice or applesauce, or NG tube) ✅✅ [label; CHEST 2021].

**AF:** 20 mg daily with the evening meal; 15 mg if CrCl 15 to 50. **VTE:** 15 mg BID x 21 days, then 20 mg daily; 10 mg daily for extended treatment. **15 and 20 mg must be taken with food** ✅ [label].
**AF:** 150 mg BID; 75 mg BID if CrCl 15 to 30. **VTE:** after 5 to 10 days of parenteral therapy, 150 mg BID. **Never open or crush** (exposure rises about 75%) ✅ [label].

**AF:** 60 mg daily; 30 mg if CrCl 15 to 50; **do not use in AF with CrCl above 95** (less effective, boxed warning). **VTE:** after 5 to 10 days parenteral; 60 mg daily (30 mg if CrCl 15 to 50, weight 60 kg or less, or certain P-gp inhibitors) ✅ [label].
Mechanical heart valves; high risk antiphospholipid syndrome (warfarin preferred); pregnancy (use LMWH); breastfeeding (labels advise against) ✅ [labels].

Avoid strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort); caution with strong inhibitors. Never combine with another anticoagulant except during planned transitions.
From a heparin infusion: start the DOAC when the infusion stops. From enoxaparin: start at the time the next enoxaparin dose would be due ✅ [labels].

Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban: low bleed risk, skip 1 day before; high bleed risk, skip 2 days before (plus the day of). Dabigatran longer when CrCl is below 50. No bridging. Restart 24 hours after low risk and 48 to 72 hours after high risk surgery ✅✅ [PAUSE; CHEST 2022].
Classic ASRA: hold 72 hours (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban), 120 hours dabigatran; restart 6 hours after catheter removal ⚠️ [5th edition now uses renal based holds; recheck].
Factor Xa inhibitors: 4F-PCC (commonly 50 units/kg or a fixed dose per protocol); andexanet withdrawn from the US market in December 2025. Dabigatran: idarucizumab 5 g IV ✅✅ [ICH 2022; TCTMD].

warfarin.title: Warfarin
sections: Blocks vitamin K recycling, so the liver cannot finish factors II, VII, IX, X (and proteins C and S). Full effect takes days; half life about 20 to 60 hours.
When it is the right choice
Mechanical valves, high risk antiphospholipid syndrome, severe kidney disease in some settings, cost.
INR 4.5 to 10: hold, recheck; routine vitamin K not needed (Crowther 2009). INR above 10: hold and give oral vitamin K 2.5 to 5 mg ✅✅ [Crowther; Sunnybrook].
Hold; vitamin K 10 mg IV (slow); 4F-PCC by INR ✅✅ [Kcentra label; Sunnybrook].
Raise INR: TMP SMX, metronidazole, fluconazole, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone. Lower INR: rifampin, carbamazepine. New illness and diet changes too.
Stop about 5 days before. AF: do not bridge (CHEST 2022, BRIDGE). Very high risk (mechanical mitral valve, clot in last 3 months): bridging decided with cardiology or hematology ✅✅ [CHEST 2022].
Teratogenic (avoid in pregnancy except special cases); compatible with breastfeeding ✅ [LactMed].
Never start warfarin alone in acute HIT; wait for platelets to recover (usually 150,000+) and overlap with a non heparin agent for at least 5 days ✅ [ASH 2018].

heparin_ufh.title: Unfractionated heparin
sections: Supercharges antithrombin to inactivate thrombin (IIa) and factor Xa.

**VTE:** 80 units/kg bolus, then 18 units/kg/h (Raschke). **ACS:** 60 units/kg (max 4,000) then 12 units/kg/h (max 1,000 units/h). **Prophylaxis:** 5,000 units SC every 8 to 12 hours ✅✅ [Raschke; label].
Actual body weight in most nomograms; some cap the dosing weight ⚠️ [protocol].
aPTT or anti Xa 6 hours after the bolus and after every rate change; platelets and hemoglobin at baseline and every 2 to 3 days (HIT).
Not renally cleared: often preferred when CrCl is very low or dialysis.
ISMP high alert; standard concentrations; never use benzyl alcohol preserved vials in neonates; read the concentration on every vial (look alike strengths).
Protamine 1 mg per 100 units given in the last 2 to 3 hours, maximum 50 mg, given slowly ✅ [ICH 2022].
Platelet fall of 50% or more around day 5 to 10, or new clots: 4Ts; stop all heparin; start argatroban or another non heparin agent ✅ [ASH 2018].

enoxaparin.title: Enoxaparin (LMWH)
sections: **Prophylaxis:** 40 mg SC daily (30 mg every 12 hours in some ortho or trauma protocols). **Treatment:** 1 mg/kg every 12 hours, or 1.5 mg/kg daily for inpatient DVT or PE ✅ [label].
CrCl below 30: treatment 1 mg/kg every 24 hours; prophylaxis 30 mg daily ✅ [label].
Actual weight for treatment; extremes of weight, pregnancy and kidney disease are where anti Xa levels help (peak about 4 hours after a dose at steady state) ✅ [label; lab].
Hold 12 hours (prophylaxis) or 24 hours (treatment) before placement or removal; next dose 4 hours after removal ✅ [label; ASRA] ⚠️ 5th edition.
Protamine partially reverses (about 60%): 1 mg per 1 mg enoxaparin within 8 hours; 0.5 mg per 1 mg if 8 to 12 hours ✅ [ICH 2022; label].
Cross reacts with HIT antibodies: do not use in HIT.
Preferred anticoagulant in pregnancy; compatible with breastfeeding ✅ [LactMed].

kcentra.title: 4F-PCC (Kcentra) and other reversal agents
sections: INR 2 to below 4: 25 units/kg (max 2,500). INR 4 to 6: 35 units/kg (max 3,500). INR above 6: 50 units/kg (max 5,000). Dosing weight capped at 100 kg. Always give **vitamin K 10 mg IV** too. Repeat dosing not studied ✅ [label].
Off label, commonly 50 units/kg or a fixed dose per protocol ✅ [ICH 2022].
Known HIT (contains heparin); DIC. Boxed warning: arterial and venous clots ✅ [label].
Per label, slow IV infusion over minutes; check St. Mary's product instructions ⚠️.

Dabigatran: **idarucizumab 5 g IV** (two 2.5 g vials). Heparin: **protamine** (1 mg per 100 units in the last 2 to 3 hours, max 50 mg). Andexanet: withdrawn from the US in December 2025 ✅✅ [ICH 2022; TCTMD].
Vitamin K plus plasma (FFP), weighing volume, or another heparin free factor product if on formulary ⚠️ [St. Mary's].

argatroban.title: Argatroban (HIT)
sections: 2 mcg/kg/min continuous infusion; 0.5 mcg/kg/min in moderate or severe hepatic impairment; adjust to aPTT 1.5 to 3 times baseline ✅ [label].
Not renally cleared (hepatic), so it works in kidney failure.
Argatroban raises the INR. Start warfarin only after platelets recover, overlap at least 5 days, and follow the label method for stopping argatroban ✅ [ASH 2018; label].
Bivalirudin, fondaparinux, or a DOAC in stable patients per ASH 2018 ✅ [ASH].

pressors.title: Vasopressors and steroids in septic shock (norepinephrine, vasopressin, epinephrine, dobutamine, hydrocortisone)
sections: Norepinephrine first to MAP 65; add vasopressin rather than raising norepinephrine; epinephrine next; dobutamine (or epinephrine) for poor heart function with low perfusion ✅✅ [SSC 2021].
Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day (50 mg IV every 6 hours or infusion) when norepinephrine or epinephrine is 0.25 mcg/kg/min or more for at least 4 hours ✅✅ [SSC 2021].
Central line preferred; short term peripheral start in a large proximal vein is acceptable while access is placed ✅ [SSC 2021]. Use St. Mary's standard concentrations only ⚠️.
Norepinephrine 4 mg/250 mL = 16 mcg/mL. For 80 kg at 0.1 mcg/kg/min: 8 mcg/min x 60 = 480 mcg/h ÷ 16 = **30 mL/h**.
Stop, aspirate, remove the catheter, restart elsewhere, elevate; **phentolamine 5 to 10 mg in 10 to 15 mL NS** infiltrated into the area, best within 12 hours ✅ [label].
Norepinephrine works and wears off within 1 to 2 minutes: never let the bag run dry; hang the next bag early.

sedation_icu.title: ICU analgesia and sedation (PADIS): fentanyl, propofol, dexmedetomidine, benzodiazepines
sections: Analgesia first, then sedation; light sedation (RASS) for most; CPOT or BPS when the patient cannot report pain ✅ [PADIS].
Screen (CAM-ICU or ICDSC); no routine antipsychotics to prevent or treat; dexmedetomidine when agitation blocks extubation ✅ [PADIS].

Hypotension; lipid calories (about 1.1 kcal/mL); triglycerides and CK on long infusions; **PRIS** risk above about 4 mg/kg/h (about 67 mcg/kg/min) and after 48 hours, especially with catecholamines or steroids: acidosis, bradycardia, rhabdomyolysis, high triglycerides; stop it ✅ [Kam 2007].
Bradycardia and hypotension; little respiratory depression.
After about 5 days or more of opioid or benzodiazepine infusions, wean rather than stop.

hyperk.title: Hyperkalemia treatment (protect, shift, remove)
sections: Calcium gluconate 1 g (10 mL of 10%) IV over 2 to 5 minutes, repeat in 5 minutes if ECG changes persist (some protocols use 3 g; calcium chloride 1 g centrally has about 3 times the calcium) ✅✅ [KDIGO; protocol] ⚠️ check order set.

Regular insulin 10 units IV with dextrose 25 g (D50 50 mL); **5 units** if kidney failure, low weight or elderly; glucose every hour for 4 to 6 hours. Nebulized albuterol 10 to 20 mg. Bicarbonate only if acidotic ✅✅ [KDIGO].
Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g or patiromer 8.4 g; loop diuretic if urine is made; dialysis ✅✅ [KDIGO].
Severe: K above 6.5, or 6.1 to 6.5 with ECG changes ✅ [KDIGO].
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone, trimethoprim, heparin, NSAIDs, potassium in fluids or TPN, missed dialysis, rhabdomyolysis.
Succinylcholine in hyperkalemia or after burns or crush (24 to 48 hours on).

hyponatremia_tx.title: Severe hyponatremia (3% saline)
sections: 3% saline 100 to 150 mL over 10 to 20 minutes, repeat up to about 3 times; goal a 4 to 6 mmol/L rise; 100 mL raises Na about 2 to 3 ✅✅ [Society for Endocrinology; ACEP].
About 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours, then 8 per 24 hours; 8 per 24 hours if high risk (alcohol use, low potassium, malnutrition, liver disease) ✅✅.
Stop hypertonic fluid; hypotonic fluid with or without desmopressin ✅.
Newer data suggest osmotic demyelination is rare; follow St. Mary's protocol ✅ [MacMillan 2023].

dka_insulin.title: DKA insulin and potassium (adults, 2024 consensus)
sections: K below 3.5: hold insulin, give potassium (about 10 mEq/h). K 3.5 to 5.0: add 10 to 20 mEq per liter of fluid and start insulin. K above 5.0: insulin only, recheck every 2 hours ✅✅ [2024 consensus].
Fixed rate regular insulin 0.1 units/kg/h, no routine bolus (only if IV access is delayed) ✅✅.
Add D5 or D10; lower insulin to 0.05 units/kg/h; keep insulin until ketones clear ✅✅.
Beta hydroxybutyrate below 0.6 and pH 7.3 or more or bicarbonate 18 or more; give SC basal insulin 1 to 2 hours before stopping the drip ✅✅.
Isotonic saline or balanced crystalloid 500 to 1,000 mL/h for 2 to 4 hours if heart and kidneys allow ✅.
Different (ISPAD 2022): no bolus, 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h after the first hour of fluids, mannitol or 3% ready for cerebral edema.

kcl_iv.title: IV potassium chloride
sections: IV push (cardiac arrest). Always a premixed bag on a pump ✅ [label].
Peripheral usually no faster than 10 mEq/h; faster needs a central line and continuous ECG per policy; label allows up to 40 mEq/h only for urgent K below 2.0 with ECG changes or paralysis ✅ [label].
About 0.1 mEq/L per 10 mEq in a stable patient (rough guide); recheck after equilibration, not from the infusing arm.
Replace low magnesium too, or potassium keeps leaking into urine.
Reduce or hold with poor urine output or rising creatinine.

sup.title: Stress ulcer prophylaxis (PPI or H2 blocker)
sections: Critically ill adults with coagulopathy, shock or chronic liver disease ✅✅ [SCCM/ASHP 2024].

When risk resolves or at ICU transfer: a common source of unneeded PPIs at discharge.

sections: Start insulin above 180; target 140 to 180 mg/dL ✅✅ [ADA; AACE].
NICE-SUGAR: 81 to 108 raised 90 day death (27.5% vs 24.9%) and severe hypoglycemia (6.8% vs 0.5%) ✅ [NICE-SUGAR].

betalactams.title: Beta lactams in the hospital (cefazolin, ceftriaxone, cefepime, piperacillin tazobactam, meropenem)
sections: Cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours (3 g for surgical prophylaxis if 120 kg+). Ceftriaxone 1 to 2 g daily (**2 g every 12 hours for meningitis**). Cefepime 2 g every 8 hours. Piperacillin tazobactam 4.5 g every 6 hours. Meropenem 1 g every 8 hours (2 g every 8 hours for meningitis) ✅ [IDSA; CAP; HAP].
Time dependent: keep levels above the MIC; prolonged infusion after the first dose suggested in sepsis ✅ [SSC 2021].
Full first dose, then adjust. **Cefepime:** adjust when CrCl is 60 or less; accumulation causes confusion, myoclonus, nonconvulsive status ✅ [FDA alert].

Cross reactivity follows the R1 side chain. Cefazolin shares no side chain with other US beta lactams. With an unconfirmed non anaphylactic penicillin history, cephalosporins can be given without testing ✅ [2022 practice parameter].

Ceftriaxone: no Pseudomonas, no Listeria, no enterococcus. Cefepime and pip tazo: Pseudomonas. Pip tazo and carbapenems already cover anaerobes (no metronidazole needed). ESBL bacteremia: carbapenem (MERINO) ✅ [MERINO].
No ceftriaxone with IV calcium or with hyperbilirubinemia.

abx_syndromes.title: Empiric regimens and durations by syndrome
sections: Ceftriaxone + azithromycin, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone; beta lactam + doxycycline if macrolide and FQ are both unsuitable; at least 5 days ✅✅ [CAP 2019].
Antipseudomonal single agent (pip tazo, cefepime, levofloxacin, meropenem) unless high risk; MRSA coverage only with risk factors; 7 days; stop vancomycin if MRSA nares negative ✅ [HAP 2016].
Ceftriaxone, a fluoroquinolone (not used in 12 months) or TMP SMX by susceptibility; 7 days (5 to 7 with FQ); no nitrofurantoin or oral fosfomycin; oral step down when improving ✅✅ [IDSA 2025].
Do not treat, except pregnancy and before urologic procedures with mucosal trauma ✅✅ [IDSA 2019].
Nonpurulent: cephalexin or cefazolin about 5 days. Abscess: drain; TMP SMX or doxycycline if over 2 cm or high risk ✅✅.

Vancomycin + ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours; add ampicillin 2 g every 4 hours if over 50, pregnant or immunocompromised; dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours started before or with the first dose ✅✅ [IDSA 2004].
MSSA: cefazolin or nafcillin/oxacillin (better than vancomycin); repeat cultures, ID consult, echo, at least 14 days IV for uncomplicated ✅ [IDSA MRSA 2011].
Fidaxomicin 200 mg BID x 10 days preferred; oral vancomycin 125 mg QID x 10 days alternative.

sections: 600 mg IV or PO every 12 hours (1:1 oral) ✅ [label].
Weak MAO inhibitor: serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, SNRIs and other serotonergic drugs; tyramine foods in large amounts ✅ [label].
Myelosuppression (platelets) usually after about 2 weeks; lactic acidosis, neuropathy with long use ✅ [label].

acls_drugs.title: Adult cardiac arrest and peri arrest drugs (AHA 2025)
sections: 1 mg IV/IO every 3 to 5 minutes: as soon as possible in asystole or PEA; after initial shocks fail in VF or pulseless VT ✅✅ [AHA 2025].
Refractory VF or pulseless VT: amiodarone 300 mg push, then 150 mg; or lidocaine 1 to 1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5 to 0.75 mg/kg. After ROSC: amiodarone 1 mg/min x 6 h, then 0.5 mg/min x 18 h ✅✅.
Calcium, bicarbonate, magnesium only for specific causes; vasopressin offers no advantage over epinephrine.

Hyperkalemia: calcium chloride 1 g (or gluconate 3 g), insulin + dextrose, bicarbonate if acidotic. Torsades: magnesium 1 to 2 g. Opioids: naloxone (ventilate first). Tricyclics: bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg. Local anesthetic: lipid 20% 1.5 mL/kg then 0.25 mL/kg/min, epinephrine 1 mcg/kg or less ✅✅ [AHA 2023 tox; ASRA].

Bradycardia: atropine 1 mg every 3 to 5 min (max 3 mg), then epinephrine 2 to 10 mcg/min, dopamine 5 to 20 mcg/kg/min or pacing. SVT: adenosine 6 mg then 12 mg rapid push with flush (3 mg with central line, transplant, dipyridamole). Anaphylaxis: epinephrine 0.5 mg IM thigh every 5 to 15 min ✅✅.
Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeat to effect; know your product (Ryanodex reconstitutes faster) ✅ [MHAUS].
SBP 90+ and MAP 65+, SpO2 92 to 98%, temperature below 37.5 °C with fever prevention ✅.

thrombolytics.title: Thrombolytics for acute ischemic stroke (tenecteplase, alteplase)
sections: Either alteplase or tenecteplase in the 4.5 hour window (2026). Selected patients up to about 9 hours or unknown onset with advanced imaging ✅✅ [AIS 2026].

**0.25 mg/kg IV bolus over 5 seconds, max 25 mg.** The STEMI dose is double: never use it. Flush with normal saline (precipitates with dextrose). Waste the excess so only the stroke dose is in the syringe.
**0.9 mg/kg, max 90 mg:** 10% bolus over 1 minute, 90% over 60 minutes; remove excess from the vial before hanging.
Tenecteplase 82 kg: 0.25 x 82 = **20.5 mg** (4.1 mL of 5 mg/mL). Alteplase 70 kg: 63 mg total; 6.3 mg bolus; 56.7 mg over 60 minutes.

BP below 185/110; glucose checked (treat if below 50); know the anticoagulant and last dose; contraindications include INR above 1.7, platelets below 100,000, therapeutic heparin or enoxaparin, recent DOAC dose; not for mild nondisabling symptoms.
BP below 180/105 for 24 hours (intensive lowering below 140 not recommended); no antithrombotics for 24 hours; neuro checks.
Labetalol 10 to 20 mg IV over 1 to 2 minutes (repeat once); nicardipine 5 mg/h, titrate 2.5 mg/h every 5 to 15 minutes (max 15); clevidipine 1 to 2 mg/h (max 21).

Angioedema (worse with ACE inhibitors): stop; methylprednisolone, diphenhydramine, famotidine; epinephrine if worsening; icatibant or C1 esterase inhibitor may be considered. Bleeding: stop; cryoprecipitate 10 units; TXA 1 g IV over 10 minutes (or aminocaproic acid).
Minor stroke or high risk TIA: aspirin + clopidogrel for 21 days (clopidogrel 300 to 600 mg load, then 75 mg), high intensity statin, glucose 140 to 180.

nimodipine.title: Nimodipine (aneurysmal SAH)
sections: 60 mg orally or by tube every 4 hours for 21 days; if BP drops, 30 mg every 2 hours ✅ [SAH 2023].
Boxed warning: deaths when capsule liquid was injected IV. Use oral or enteral syringes that cannot connect to IV lines, labeled oral only ✅.
If used, levetiracetam is preferred over phenytoin ✅ [SAH 2023].

trauma_drugs.title: Trauma bay drugs (TXA, calcium, RSI, osmotherapy, antibiotics, tetanus)
sections: 1 g IV over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours, only within 3 hours of injury (later may harm). Ask EMS what was given ✅✅ [CRASH-2]. TBI: CRASH-3 benefit in mild to moderate TBI within 3 hours ✅ [CRASH-3].
Close to 1:1:1; calcium chloride 1 g (central) or calcium gluconate 3 g guided by ionized calcium (citrate binds calcium); watch potassium and temperature ✅ [PROPPR].

Ketamine 1 to 2 mg/kg or etomidate 0.3 mg/kg (avoid full dose propofol in shock); rocuronium 1 to 1.2 mg/kg (sugammadex 16 mg/kg for immediate reversal); succinylcholine 1 to 1.5 mg/kg but never in hyperkalemia or 24 to 48 hours after burns, crush or spinal cord injury; start analgesia and sedation right after the tube.
Mannitol 0.25 to 1 g/kg, or 3% 250 mL, or 23.4% 30 mL central only (ISMP high alert); seizure prophylaxis 7 days; no steroids ✅ [BTF].
Cefazolin 2 g (3 g if 120 kg+) within 1 hour; type III add gram negative coverage; penicillin for farm or soil contamination per protocol ⚠️.
Clean minor wound: booster if more than 10 years. Dirty wound: more than 5 years. Dirty + unknown or fewer than 3 doses: Tdap plus TIG 250 units IM ✅✅ [CDC].
Parkland: 4 mL x kg x %TBSA of lactated Ringer's over 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn.
Enoxaparin prophylaxis once bleeding is stable (often 24 to 48 hours); multimodal pain for ribs; thiamine before glucose in alcohol use.

neonatal.title: Neonatal dosing essentials
sections: GA = weeks at birth. PNA = days since birth. PMA = GA + weeks since birth. Many intervals depend on PMA and PNA.
Calculate mg/kg on every dose; leading zero, no trailing zero; mg/kg/dose vs mg/kg/day; preservative free products (benzyl alcohol causes gasping syndrome); read heparin concentrations every time.
Ventilation first. Epinephrine 0.1 mg/mL: IV/UVC 0.02 mg/kg (0.01 to 0.03); ETT 0.1 mg/kg (0.05 to 0.1); every 3 to 5 minutes. Normal saline 10 mL/kg over 5 to 10 minutes ✅✅ [NRP; LHSC].
Vitamin K 0.5 to 1 mg IM; erythromycin 0.5% eye ointment; hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours (+ HBIG within 12 hours if mom HBsAg positive).
Early onset: ampicillin + gentamicin (unit chart). Meningitis: ampicillin + cefepime or ceftazidime (cefotaxime unavailable) ⚠️. HSV: acyclovir 20 mg/kg every 8 hours.
Never with IV calcium in neonates; avoid in hyperbilirubinemia ✅ [label; AAP 2022].
Citrate 20 mg/kg load, then 5 to 10 mg/kg daily; 2 mg citrate = 1 mg base.
D10W 2 mL/kg, then infusion; never D50.
Calcium and phosphate solubility curve; phosphate early, calcium last; cysteine helps; independent double check.

sections: mg/kg, never above the adult dose. Measured weight in kg.

Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL), max 1 mg; amiodarone 5 mg/kg (max 300), up to 15 mg/kg; lidocaine 1 mg/kg; adenosine 0.1 mg/kg (max 6) then 0.2 mg/kg (max 12); atropine 0.02 mg/kg (max 0.5); calcium chloride 20 mg/kg; dextrose 0.5 to 1 g/kg ✅ [PALS 2025].

Midazolam IM 10 mg (over 40 kg) or 5 mg (13 to 40 kg); lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4), repeat once. Then levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4,500), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (max 1,500), or valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3,000) ✅✅ [AES; ESETT].
No bolus; insulin 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h after the first hour of fluids; mannitol 0.5 to 1 g/kg or 3% 2.5 to 5 mL/kg ready ✅ [ISPAD 2022].
Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg every 6 hours (max 75 mg/kg/day, 4 g); ibuprofen 10 mg/kg every 6 to 8 hours (6 months+); Holliday Segar 4/2/1; isotonic maintenance fluids ✅ [AAP 2018].
After 5+ days of opioid or benzodiazepine infusions: WAT-1 scoring and a wean (enteral methadone, lorazepam).

sections: Training and knowledge every 12 months; garbing (gloved fingertip: 3 passes at 0 CFU to start) and aseptic technique (media fill + fingertip above 3 CFU fails + surface sample) every 6 months for Category 1 and 2, every 3 months for Category 3 ✅✅ [USP 797; summary].
Dirty to clean: shoe covers, hair cover, mask, wash 30 seconds, gown, sterile gloves, sterile 70% IPA often.
ISO 5 hood, ISO 7 buffer, ISO 8 ante (ISO 7 if it opens to negative pressure); buffer positive at least 0.02 inch water column; never block first air.
Certification every 6 months; surface sampling at least monthly; viable air at least every 6 months; sporicidal cleaning at least monthly.

Immediate use: 3 products max, start within 4 hours. Category 1: 12 hours room temperature, 24 hours refrigerated. Category 2 (sterile ingredients, no sterility test): 4 days, 10 days, 45 days frozen; with a nonsterile ingredient: 1, 4, 45. Always the shorter of sterility and stability.
Single dose: 12 hours if punctured in ISO 5 (1 hour outside). Multiple dose: 28 days unless labeled otherwise.
Containment hood in a negative pressure room; double ASTM D6978 gloves; chemo gown; CSTD; spill kit ✅ [USP 800].

sections: Insulin, anticoagulants, concentrated electrolytes, opioids, neuromuscular blockers, chemotherapy, magnesium, oxytocin, TXA injection (added 2024). Fix with standard concentrations, pump libraries, premixes, separate storage ✅✅ [ISMP].
No U, IU, QD, QOD, MS, MSO4, MgSO4, trailing zeros; always a leading zero.
National Performance Goals replaced the NPSGs; medication management covers labeling, anticoagulants, pharmacist review, override review, standard concentrations, stewardship ✅ [NPG].

Renew every 2 years, 30 hours, 2 h medication errors, 2 h controlled substances, no live hours since 2025; immunization 3 h; consultant 24 h. E-FORCSE reporting by the next business day ✅✅ [Board].

verify_basics.title: Order verification basics (topic card)
sections: Patient (age, weight, allergies with reaction, pregnancy or breastfeeding), indication, labs (SCr, platelets, others by drug), drug and dose, duplicates and interactions, then decide.
Cockcroft Gault: (140 minus age) x weight in kg / (72 x SCr), x 0.85 if female. Think about which weight in obesity, very low weights, and changing creatinine.
Every allergy needs a reaction. Clarify vague labels; document tolerated drugs.
The prescriber (or covering prescriber) changes orders; the nurse gives information; your supervisor helps when you disagree. Use SBAR.
Life threatening now, then time sensitive (first doses, STAT), then routine, then questions.
Get background, find the real question, search (Trissel's or King for Y site; LactMed; Lexicomp or Micromedex), answer clearly, document. No data for a Y site pair means do not run them together.

evidence.title: Reading trials (topic card)
sections: ARR = control rate minus treatment rate. RRR = ARR / control rate. NNT (or NNH) = 1 / ARR.
NICE-SUGAR 27.5 vs 24.9%: ARI 2.6, NNH about 38. AMPLIFY-EXT 8.8 vs 1.7%: ARR 7.1, NNT about 14. BRIDGE bleeding 3.2 vs 1.3%: NNH about 53.
"Not met" means not proven as good, not proven worse.
MUE targets: high alert, high cost, high volume, new alert. Fix with order sets and pump limits. Ask the IRB before collecting data if you may present ✅ [ASHP MUE].
